text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam bourse knew about breaches of bourse regulations by stockbroker Regio Effekt in 1992. (p1)
- Brewer Grolsch shares tumble more than 20 percent on poor 1996 results. (p1)
- Anglo/Dutch publisher Reed-Elsevier boosts profit margin. (p1)
- Builder Volker Stevin and Kondor Wessels, who are to merge, seek to open up new markets. (p1)
- Technical wholesaler Econosto is forecasting 30-45 percent profits increase in 1997. (p3)
- Automation firm Ordina books 43 percent higher net in 1996 at Dfl 16.6 million. (p3)
- Car industry supplier Polynorm 1996 net profit pressured by weak German market. (p4)
- Participation group NPM takes a minority stake in corporate finance consultant Van den Boom Group (VDBG). (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Parliament hesitates about allowing experiment with free heroin for heavily addicted. (p1)
- Justice minister Winnie Sorgdrager is against higher sentences for selling soft drugs. (p1)
- Pyramid games appear to be very popular in the Netherlands. (p2)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) pays 88 million guilders to become full owner of cable exploiting company Casema. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- KPN, bank insurer ING and builder NBM Amstelland join forces with public transport group VSN to fight traffic jams. (p1)
- More than 90 percent of the Dutch get their cash from money dispensing machines, research shows. (p10)
- Philips Electronics sells mechatronics unit to its management. (p35)
- ING targets at experienced investors for its IT-fund that is to be launched on March 27. (p37)
TROUW
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo angers China by pleading for human rights. (p6)
- Grand hotel Krasnapolsky takes over city castle Oudaen in Utrecht. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Project group VERM advices a smaller extension of Rotterdam port on the second Maasvlakte. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM is to increase number of flights by eight percent this summer. (p10) --Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
